phrases.translation: Alif-Lãm-Ra. These are the verses of the Book, rich in wisdom
phrases.explanation: The surah opens with the separated letters Alif-Lãm-Ra, whose full meaning is not explained in this verse. Their sound marks the opening of revelation and invites the listener to attend carefully. The verses are described as a Book rich in wisdom. Its guidance is presented as purposeful and profound, offering insight rather than empty speech.

phrases.translation: Is it astonishing to people that We have sent revelation to a man from among themselves, ˹instructing him,˺ “Warn humanity and give good news to the believers that they will have an honourable status with their Lord.”? Yet the disbelievers said, “Indeed, this ˹man˺ is clearly a magician!”
phrases.explanation: People wonder that revelation came through a man from among them. The message tells him to warn humanity and give believers the good news of an honourable standing with their Lord. The disbelievers call the messenger a magician. Their accusation rejects the message by attacking its bearer, rather than answering the warning and promise it brings.

phrases.translation: Surely your Lord is Allah Who created the heavens and the earth in six Days, then established Himself on the Throne, conducting every affair.
phrases.explanation: Allah created the heavens and earth and governs every affair. The verse joins creation with continuing authority, presenting the world as sustained by one Lord rather than left without direction.

phrases.translation: None can intercede except by His permission. That is Allah—your Lord, so worship Him ˹alone˺. Will you not then be mindful
phrases.explanation: No one can intercede without Allah’s permission. The statement limits every claim of independent spiritual authority and makes clear that all mediation remains under His control. Because Allah alone is Lord, people are told to worship Him and remain mindful. The verse turns its account of creation and sovereignty into a direct call to devotion.

phrases.translation: To Him is your return all together. Allah’s promise is ˹always˺ true. Indeed, He originates the creation then resurrects it so that He may justly reward those who believe and do good.
phrases.explanation: Everyone returns to Allah, and His promise is true. The certainty of return grounds the verse’s warning and assurance in a final accountability that no one can avoid. Allah originates creation and will bring it back so that believers who do good receive a just reward. Resurrection is linked to moral accountability, not merely to repeating the act of creation.

phrases.translation: But those who disbelieve will have a boiling drink and a painful punishment for their disbelief
phrases.explanation: Those who disbelieve face a boiling drink and painful punishment because of their disbelief. The verse presents this consequence as a response to rejection, in contrast with the reward promised to the faithful.

phrases.translation: He is the One Who made the sun a radiant source and the moon a reflected light, with precisely ordained phases, so that you may know the number of years and calculation ˹of time˺. Allah did not create all this except for a purpose. He makes the signs clear for people of knowledge
phrases.explanation: The sun is described as radiant and the moon as reflecting light. Their different roles make the sky a visible pattern through which people can observe and measure time. The moon’s measured phases allow people to count years and calculate time. The verse links familiar natural cycles with practical knowledge used to order human life. Allah created these signs for a purpose and makes them clear for people of knowledge. Reflection on the heavens can lead beyond observation toward recognition of intention and wisdom.

phrases.translation: Surely in the alternation of the day and the night, and in all that Allah has created in the heavens and the earth, there are truly signs for those mindful ˹of Him˺
phrases.explanation: The alternation of day and night and the created world provide signs for people mindful of Allah. Regular change, variety, and order invite reflection on the One who sustains creation.

phrases.translation: Indeed, those who do not expect to meet Us, being pleased and content with this worldly life, and who are heedless of Our signs
phrases.explanation: The verse describes people who do not expect to meet Allah and feel satisfied with worldly life alone. Their contentment becomes a barrier when it leaves no room for accountability beyond the present. They are heedless of Allah’s signs. The issue is not simply enjoying life, but refusing to notice guidance that could redirect their priorities.

phrases.translation: they will have the Fire as a home because of what they have committed
phrases.explanation: The Fire becomes the home of those described in the previous verse, because of what they have committed. The outcome is connected to their chosen heedlessness rather than presented as an unexplained fate.

phrases.translation: Surely those who believe and do good, their Lord will guide them ˹to Paradise˺ through their faith, rivers will flow under their feet in the Gardens of Bliss
phrases.explanation: Those who believe and do good are guided by their Lord through their faith. Faith is presented as a living orientation that leads a person toward Allah’s promised destination. Their destination is Paradise, pictured with rivers flowing beneath the Gardens of Bliss. The imagery conveys lasting security and delight as the reward for faith and good conduct.

phrases.translation: in which their prayer will be, “Glory be to You, O Allah!” and their greeting will be, “Peace!” and their closing prayer will be, “All praise is for Allah—Lord of all worlds!”
phrases.explanation: The believers’ prayer in Paradise glorifies Allah. Their first words express recognition of His perfection and gratitude for the blessed place they have entered. Their greeting is peace, a word of safety and welcome. The verse portrays Paradise as a community where hostility and fear have given way to tranquillity. Their closing prayer praises Allah, Lord of all worlds. Gratitude remains the fitting response to His mercy and the joy of the Gardens.

phrases.translation: If Allah were to hasten evil for people as they wish to hasten good,
phrases.explanation: People often want good to arrive quickly, but if harm came just as quickly whenever they demanded it, they would be ruined. The verse highlights the danger of impulsive wishes.

phrases.translation: they would have certainly been doomed. But We leave those who do not expect to meet Us to wander blindly in their defiance
phrases.explanation: The warning shows that immediate fulfillment of every demand would not be mercy. Restraint protects people from consequences they may request without understanding. Those who do not expect to meet Allah are left to wander in defiance. The verse describes the result of refusing accountability, as choices increasingly direct them away from guidance.

phrases.translation: Whenever someone is touched by hardship, they cry out to Us, whether lying on their side, sitting, or standing.
phrases.explanation: When hardship touches a person, they call on Allah in every posture, whether lying down, sitting, or standing. Distress can strip away pride and remind people of their need for help.

phrases.translation: But when We relieve their hardship, they return to their old ways as if they had never cried to Us to remove any hardship! This is how the misdeeds of the transgressors have been made appealing to them
phrases.explanation: After relief comes, they return to their former ways as though they had never prayed. The contrast exposes how quickly gratitude and remembrance can fade once danger passes. The verse says wrongdoing has been made appealing to transgressors. Repeatedly ignoring guidance can distort judgment until harmful habits seem normal or attractive.

phrases.translation: We surely destroyed ˹other˺ peoples before you when they did wrong, and their messengers came to them with clear proofs but they would not believe! This is how We reward the wicked people
phrases.explanation: Earlier peoples were destroyed after wrongdoing, even though messengers brought them clear proofs. The verse presents the messengers’ warnings as an opportunity their communities chose not to accept. Those peoples persisted in disbelief despite the evidence. The repeated refusal, rather than a lack of warning, is central to the lesson drawn from their history. This is how the wicked are repaid. The verse uses past communities as a warning to the audience that injustice and rejection carry serious consequences.

phrases.translation: Then We made you their successors in the land to see how you would act
phrases.explanation: After earlier peoples, the audience is made successor in the land and given a chance to act. Inheritance is therefore a responsibility and a test, not simply a privilege without accountability.

phrases.translation: When Our clear revelations are recited to them, those who do not expect to meet Us say ˹to the Prophet˺, “Bring us a different Quran or make some changes in it.”
phrases.explanation: Those who do not expect to meet Allah demand another Quran or changes to the revelation. Their request seeks a message tailored to their wishes rather than guidance that challenges them.

phrases.translation: Say ˹to them˺, “It is not for me to change it on my own. I only follow what is revealed to me. I fear, if I were to disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day.”
phrases.explanation: The Prophet answers that he cannot alter the Quran on his own and only follows what is revealed. His role is to convey the message faithfully, not rewrite it for approval. He fears punishment if he disobeys his Lord on the tremendous Day. The answer grounds the refusal in obedience and accountability, not in personal stubbornness.

phrases.translation: Say, “Had Allah willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made it known to you.
phrases.explanation: The Prophet says that, had Allah willed otherwise, he would not have recited the revelation or made it known. The message is therefore presented as something entrusted to him, not invented for advantage.

phrases.translation: I had lived my whole life among you before this ˹revelation˺. Do you not understand?”
phrases.explanation: He had lived among the people for his whole life before the revelation came. The reminder invites them to consider their own knowledge of him when judging the claim that he fabricated it. The question asks whether they will understand this evidence. The verse calls for reflection on the messenger’s history and the source of the message rather than reflexive accusation.

phrases.translation: Who does more wrong than those who fabricate lies against Allah or deny His revelations? Indeed, the wicked will never succeed
phrases.explanation: The verse asks who could do greater wrong than those who lie about Allah or deny His revelations. It treats false claims about the divine and rejection of guidance as grave moral acts. The wicked will never succeed. The statement contrasts temporary attempts to distort the truth with the lasting failure that follows wrongdoing.

phrases.translation: They worship besides Allah others who can neither harm nor benefit them, and say, “These are our intercessors with Allah.”
phrases.explanation: The people described worship others who cannot harm or benefit them. The verse questions the logic of turning to beings with no independent power for protection or advantage. They claim these beings are their intercessors with Allah. The verse presents this as their justification, then challenges whether they can truly establish such a claim.

phrases.translation: Ask ˹them, O Prophet˺, “Are you informing Allah of something He does not know in the heavens or the earth? Glorified and Exalted is He above what they associate ˹with Him˺!”
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is told to ask whether they are informing Allah of something unknown in heaven or earth. The question exposes the weakness of attributing partners or intercessors without divine authority. Allah is exalted above what people associate with Him. The closing rejects any description that compromises His uniqueness or assigns Him partners.

phrases.translation: Humanity was once nothing but a single community ˹of believers˺, but then they differed.
phrases.explanation: Humanity is described as once united in belief, before disagreement arose. The verse points to an original shared direction and makes later divisions a matter for reflection. People later disagreed. The brief statement acknowledges division without treating every difference as equally blameworthy or explaining it as an excuse to abandon guidance.

phrases.translation: Had it not been for a prior decree from your Lord, their differences would have been settled ˹at once˺
phrases.explanation: A prior decree from Allah delayed the settling of their differences. The verse places the timing of judgment within divine wisdom rather than assuming every dispute must be resolved immediately.

phrases.translation: They ask, “Why has no ˹other˺ sign been sent down to him from his Lord?” Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “˹The knowledge of˺ the unseen is with Allah alone. So wait! I too am waiting with you.”
phrases.explanation: People ask why another sign has not been sent to the Prophet. The request treats visible signs as a condition for belief, despite the revelations already presented. The unseen belongs to Allah alone. The Prophet does not control when signs or future events are disclosed, because knowledge of what is hidden rests with Allah. The Prophet says that he and his audience will wait. The answer leaves the matter with Allah and calls people to face the outcome rather than dictate its timing.

phrases.translation: When We give people a taste of mercy after being afflicted with a hardship, they swiftly devise plots against Our revelations!
phrases.explanation: After people experience hardship, Allah gives them a taste of mercy. The contrast should lead to gratitude, yet some instead plot against the revelations that call them to guidance. They respond to relief by scheming against Allah’s signs. The verse exposes how temporary comfort can make people forget their dependence and resist the message that challenged them.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Allah is swifter in devising ˹punishment˺. Surely Our messenger-angels record whatever you devise.”
phrases.explanation: Allah is swifter in devising a consequence than they are in plotting. The warning reminds them that human schemes cannot outpace divine judgment. The messenger-angels record whatever they devise. Their actions are not lost or hidden, even when their plans are meant to undermine the truth.

phrases.translation: He is the One Who enables you to travel through land and sea. And it so happens that you are on ships, sailing with a favourable wind, to the passengers’ delight.
phrases.explanation: Allah enables people to travel by land and sea. The verse begins with an ordinary blessing, reminding travelers that their ability to move safely depends on Him. A favourable wind carries the ships, and the passengers rejoice. Calm conditions can make a journey seem fully secure, even though people do not control the forces around them.

phrases.translation: Suddenly, the ships are overcome by a gale wind and those on board are overwhelmed by waves from every side, and they assume they are doomed. They cry out to Allah ˹alone˺ in sincere devotion, “If You save us from this, we will certainly be grateful.”
phrases.explanation: A gale and waves suddenly surround the ship, leaving its passengers convinced they may die. The abrupt danger shows how quickly apparent security can disappear. In danger, the passengers call on Allah alone with sincere devotion. Fear strips away the false sense of self-sufficiency and turns them directly to their Creator. They promise gratitude if rescued. The verse prepares the contrast with what happens after safety returns, asking whether their devotion will last beyond the crisis.

phrases.translation: But as soon as He rescues them, they transgress in the land unjustly. O humanity! Your transgression is only against your own souls.
phrases.explanation: After rescue, people may return to wrongdoing and exceed proper limits. The verse contrasts their urgent prayer at sea with their conduct once the danger has passed. Transgression ultimately harms the transgressor. The warning tells humanity that injustice may affect others, but its moral cost and final consequences return to the one who commits it.

phrases.translation: ˹There is only˺ brief enjoyment in this worldly life, then to Us is your return, and then We will inform you of what you used to do
phrases.explanation: Worldly enjoyment is brief. The verse does not deny that life contains pleasure, but places it within a short horizon before everyone returns to Allah. Allah will then inform people of what they did. The prospect of judgment makes present choices important, even when worldly wrongdoing seems to bring immediate advantage.

phrases.translation: The life of this world is just like rain We send down from the sky, producing a mixture of plants which humans and animals consume. Then just as the earth looks its best, perfectly beautified, and its people think they have full control over it,
phrases.explanation: Rain produces plants that feed both people and animals. The image begins with familiar abundance, showing how life and provision can flourish through conditions beyond human control. The earth becomes beautiful and its people imagine that they command it. The verse highlights the false confidence that can grow when prosperity appears secure.

phrases.translation: there comes to it Our command by night or by day, so We mow it down as if it never flourished yesterday! This is how We make the signs clear for people who reflect
phrases.explanation: Allah’s command arrives by night or day and the flourishing land is cut down. The sudden reversal illustrates how quickly worldly beauty and control can vanish. These signs are made clear for people who reflect. The lesson is not to despise creation, but to look beyond its temporary display and consider the power and wisdom behind it.

phrases.translation: And Allah invites ˹all˺ to the Home of Peace and guides whoever He wills to the Straight Path
phrases.explanation: Allah invites everyone to the Home of Peace, a description of the lasting safety and well-being promised in the Hereafter. The invitation is broad, even though people respond differently. He guides whoever He wills to the Straight Path. Guidance comes from Allah and leads toward the right way, calling people to respond with trust and obedience.

phrases.translation: Those who do good will have the finest reward and ˹even˺ more. Neither gloom nor disgrace will cover their faces. It is they who will be the residents of Paradise. They will be there forever
phrases.explanation: Those who do good receive the finest reward and something beyond it. The promise points to divine generosity that exceeds what a person can earn or fully imagine. Neither gloom nor disgrace covers them. The image conveys inward joy and public honour, in contrast with the shame and fear described for those who do evil. They live in Paradise forever. The verse presents lasting residence there as the outcome for those who believe and do good, not a temporary reward that can be lost.

phrases.translation: As for those who commit evil, the reward of an evil deed is its equivalent. Humiliation will cover them—with no one to protect them from Allah—as if their faces were covered with patches of the night’s deep darkness. It is they who will be the residents of the Fire. They will be there forever
phrases.explanation: An evil deed receives its equivalent, establishing proportion in judgment. The verse does not describe punishment as arbitrary or greater than the wrongdoing it answers. Humiliation covers the wrongdoers, with no protector to shield them from Allah. The darkness on their faces pictures the exposure and shame of a final reckoning. They become residents of the Fire forever. The verse contrasts their destination with the believers’ Paradise and stresses the seriousness of persistent evil.

phrases.translation: ˹Consider˺ the Day We will gather them all together then say to those who associated others ˹with Allah in worship˺, “Stay in your places—you and your associate-gods.” We will separate them from each other, and their associate-gods will say, “It was not us that you worshipped
phrases.explanation: On the Day of gathering, those who associated partners with Allah are told to stay with the beings they worshipped. The scene brings their claim into public judgment. The people and their alleged associate-gods are separated. The separation exposes that the relationship they imagined cannot provide the support they expected. The associate-gods deny that the people worshipped them. Their response leaves the worshippers without the intercession or loyalty they had assumed.

phrases.translation: Allah is sufficient as a Witness between each of us that we were totally unaware of your worship.”
phrases.explanation: Allah is invoked as witness between the worshippers and those they associated with Him. The statement presents the matter as open to truthful judgment, not dependent on competing claims. The alleged gods say they were unaware of the worship directed to them. Their denial confirms that the worshippers relied on beings who could neither authorize nor answer their devotion.

phrases.translation: Then and there every soul will face ˹the consequences of˺ what it had done. They all will be returned to Allah—their True Master. And whatever ˹gods˺ they fabricated will fail them
phrases.explanation: Every soul faces the consequences of its own actions. The scene leaves no room for hiding behind another person’s record or claiming that deeds have no moral weight. All are returned to Allah, their True Master. The title contrasts His real authority with the powerless objects people had treated as gods. The fabricated gods fail their worshippers. False reliance cannot rescue anyone at judgment, when the truth of every person’s choices becomes clear.

phrases.translation: Ask ˹them, O Prophet˺, “Who provides for you from heaven and earth?
phrases.explanation: The first question asks who provides from the heavens and earth. It directs attention to the sources of sustenance and invites the audience to acknowledge the One who supplies them.

phrases.translation: Who owns ˹your˺ hearing and sight? Who brings forth the living from the dead and the dead from the living?
phrases.explanation: The questions turn to hearing and sight, abilities people often take for granted. Recognizing their source makes it harder to claim that life operates independently of Allah. Allah brings forth the living from the dead and the dead from the living. The cycle of life and death is presented as another sign of His power over creation.

phrases.translation: And who conducts every affair?” They will ˹surely˺ say, “Allah.” Say, “Will you not then fear ˹Him˺
phrases.explanation: The audience is expected to answer that Allah conducts every affair. Their own admission supplies the basis for the Prophet’s next question about whether they will be mindful. The verse challenges them to fear and revere the Lord they have acknowledged. Belief in Allah’s power should shape conduct, not remain only a verbal answer.

phrases.translation: That is Allah—your True Lord. So what is beyond the truth except falsehood? How can you then be turned away?”
phrases.explanation: Allah is identified as the True Lord. The phrase summarizes the answers just given and distinguishes real divine authority from the claims made for other beings. If Allah is the truth, what lies beyond the truth is falsehood. The contrast asks listeners to evaluate their beliefs rather than treating truth and error as equally grounded. The verse asks how people can be turned away from the truth. The question expresses astonishment at abandoning what their own answers have already confirmed.

phrases.translation: And so your Lord’s decree has been proven true against the rebellious—that they will never believe
phrases.explanation: Allah’s decree is proven true against the rebellious: they will not believe. The verse describes the settled outcome of persistent rebellion and should be read with the passage’s earlier invitations to accept guidance.

phrases.translation: Ask ˹them, O Prophet˺, “Can any of your associate-gods originate creation and then resurrect it?” Say, “˹Only˺ Allah originates creation and then resurrects it. How can you then be deluded ˹from the truth˺?”
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is told to ask whether the associate-gods can originate creation and bring it back. The question tests their supposed power against the most fundamental acts of creation. Only Allah originates creation and resurrects it. The verse then asks how people can be deluded from this truth, challenging them to reconsider the gods they claim to follow.

phrases.translation: Ask ˹them, O Prophet˺, “Can any of your associate-gods guide to the truth?” Say, “˹Only˺ Allah guides to the truth.”
phrases.explanation: The Prophet asks whether any associate-god can guide people to the truth. The question compares the alleged gods with the guidance that people need to find their way. Allah alone guides to the truth. This answer identifies Him as the reliable source of direction, rather than leaving people to depend on powerless beings.

phrases.translation: Who then is more worthy to be followed: the One Who guides to the truth or those who cannot find the way unless guided? What is the matter with you? How do you judge
phrases.explanation: The verse asks whether the one who guides to truth is more worthy to be followed than those who cannot find their way without guidance. Its comparison makes the difference in authority plain. The closing questions challenge the audience’s judgment. They are urged to recognize the contradiction in following what cannot guide while turning away from the One who does.

phrases.translation: Most of them follow nothing but ˹inherited˺ assumptions. ˹And˺ surely assumptions can in no way replace the truth. Allah is indeed All-Knowing of what they do
phrases.explanation: Many people follow inherited assumptions rather than knowledge. The verse warns that familiar beliefs are not automatically true merely because they have been repeated across generations. Assumption cannot replace truth. The warning encourages people to distinguish evidence from conjecture when making claims about Allah and worship. Allah knows what people do. Their actions and the beliefs guiding them are fully known to Him, giving weight to the warning against careless assumptions.

phrases.translation: It is not ˹possible˺ for this Quran to have been produced by anyone other than Allah. In fact, it is a confirmation of what came before, and an explanation of the Scripture. It is, without a doubt, from the Lord of all worlds
phrases.explanation: The Quran is not presented as something any person could have produced independently of Allah. The verse asserts its divine origin against the charge that it was fabricated. It confirms what came before and explains the Scripture. The verse connects the Quran with earlier revelation while describing its role in clarifying guidance. The Quran is without doubt from the Lord of all worlds. The conclusion presents its source as universal and divine, not the product of a local human invention.

phrases.translation: Or do they claim, “He made it up!”? Tell them ˹O Prophet˺, “Produce one sûrah like it then, and seek help from whoever you can—other than Allah—if what you say is true!”
phrases.explanation: Some accuse the Prophet of inventing the Quran. The verse states their charge directly so that it can be answered with a challenge to produce something comparable. They are invited to produce one surah like it and call on any helpers besides Allah if their claim is true. The challenge asks them to substantiate the accusation rather than repeat it.

phrases.translation: In fact, they ˹hastily˺ rejected the Book without comprehending it and before the fulfilment of its warnings. Similarly, those before them were in denial.
phrases.explanation: The people reject the Book before understanding it and before its warnings have been fulfilled. The verse criticizes a hasty judgment made without careful engagement or patience. Earlier peoples also denied their messengers. The comparison shows that the audience’s response repeats a familiar pattern of rejecting warnings before considering their truth.

phrases.translation: See then what was the end of the wrongdoers
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is told to look at the end of wrongdoers. History supplies a warning about where persistent denial can lead, rather than proof that every critic shares the same fate.

phrases.translation: Some of them will ˹eventually˺ believe in it; others will not. And your Lord knows best the corruptors
phrases.explanation: People respond differently: some will eventually believe in the Quran while others remain unwilling. The verse recognizes this diversity without requiring the Prophet to control every person’s choice. Allah knows best who corrupts. Human beings may not see every motive or future action, but Allah fully knows those who persist in causing corruption.

phrases.translation: If they deny you, then say,
phrases.explanation: If people deny the Prophet, he is told to speak clearly about responsibility. His conduct belongs to him and theirs to them. Their rejection does not make him answerable for their choices.

phrases.translation: “My deeds are mine and your deeds are yours. You are free of what I do and I am free of what you do!”
phrases.explanation: The Prophet’s deeds are his own, while the deniers’ deeds belong to them. The verse establishes a boundary between conveying guidance and forcing another person to accept it. Each side is free of the other’s deeds. This does not praise disbelief. It makes clear that people will be accountable for their own response to the message.

phrases.translation: Some of them listen to what you say, but can you make the deaf hear even though they do not understand
phrases.explanation: Some people hear the Prophet’s words but do not understand their guidance. The image describes a failure of receptivity, not a physical disability or a lack of ordinary hearing. The rhetorical question asks whether the Prophet can make such people truly hear. He can convey the message, but cannot force sincere understanding into someone who refuses it.

phrases.translation: And some of them look at you, but can you guide the blind even though they cannot see
phrases.explanation: Some people look directly at the Prophet but do not recognize the truth he brings. Seeing him physically does not guarantee that they will understand or accept his message. The image of guiding the blind describes people who will not see guidance, not people with visual disabilities. The Prophet cannot compel a person’s heart to follow what it refuses to recognize.

phrases.translation: Indeed, Allah does not wrong people in the least, but it is people who wrong themselves
phrases.explanation: Allah does not wrong people at all. The verse rejects the idea that people’s suffering or final judgment comes from divine injustice. People wrong themselves through their own choices. Their actions carry consequences, so the responsibility for rejecting guidance or committing injustice cannot be shifted onto Allah.

phrases.translation: On the Day He will gather them, it will be as if they had not stayed ˹in the world˺ except for an hour of a day,
phrases.explanation: At the gathering, worldly life will seem as brief as an hour of a day. In the presence of the Hereafter, the time people treated as their whole horizon will appear fleeting.

phrases.translation: ˹as though they were only˺ getting to know one another. Lost indeed will be those who denied the meeting with Allah, and were not ˹rightly˺ guided
phrases.explanation: They seem to have spent that short time only getting to know one another. The image underscores how quickly earthly relationships and routines pass before final accountability. Those who denied meeting Allah are truly lost and were not rightly guided. Their loss comes from rejecting the return that gives lasting significance to life’s choices.

phrases.translation: Whether We show you ˹O Prophet˺ some of what We threaten them with, or cause you to die ˹before that˺, to Us is their return and Allah is a Witness over what they do
phrases.explanation: The Prophet may witness some of the threatened consequences, or he may die before they occur. The warning does not depend on his personally seeing every outcome. Whether or not the Prophet sees events unfold, the people will return to Allah. Their accountability is certain even if its timing lies beyond his lifetime. Allah witnesses what they do. The verse reassures the Prophet that no deed is overlooked and that judgment rests with the One who knows their actions fully.

phrases.translation: And for every community there is a messenger. After their messenger has come, judgment is passed on them in all fairness, and they are not wronged
phrases.explanation: Every community receives a messenger. The verse presents revelation as a recurring means of guidance across peoples rather than a message intended for only one group. After the messenger comes, judgment is passed fairly and no one is wronged. The order of warning and judgment underlines that accountability follows an opportunity to hear guidance.

phrases.translation: They ask ˹the believers˺, “When will this threat come to pass if what you say is true?”
phrases.explanation: The questioners demand to know when the promised threat will arrive if the believers are truthful. Their challenge focuses on timing, while the passage has already emphasized that a delay does not cancel accountability.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “I have no power to benefit or protect myself, except by the Will of Allah.” For each community there is an appointed term. When their time arrives, they cannot delay it for a moment, nor could they advance it
phrases.explanation: The Prophet has no independent power to benefit or protect himself, since everything is subject to Allah’s will. The statement rejects claims that he controls outcomes apart from his Lord. Each community has an appointed term. The verse presents the timing of collective outcomes as set by Allah rather than something people can dictate through demands. When the appointed time comes, people cannot delay or advance it. The warning answers those who demand that judgment arrive on their schedule.

phrases.translation: Tell them ˹O Prophet˺, “Imagine if His torment were to overcome you by night or day—do the wicked realize what they are ˹really˺ asking Him to hasten
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is told to ask whether the wicked understand what they are asking to hasten: a torment that could come by night or by day. Their challenge ignores the danger of its fulfillment.

phrases.translation: Will you believe in it only after it has overtaken you? Now? But you always wanted to hasten it!”
phrases.explanation: The verse asks whether they will believe only after the promised punishment arrives. Belief forced by seeing the consequence is contrasted with responding before it is too late. They had repeatedly wanted the threat hastened. The question exposes the contradiction between demanding punishment in defiance and facing it when it becomes real.

phrases.translation: Then the wrongdoers will be told, “Taste the torment of eternity! Are you not rewarded except for what you used to commit?”
phrases.explanation: The wrongdoers are told to taste the lasting torment. The direct command makes the judgment vivid, confronting them with the consequence they had treated as unreal. They are asked whether they are being repaid for anything other than what they used to commit. The verse links the punishment to their own deeds rather than to arbitrary treatment.

phrases.translation: They ask you ˹O Prophet˺, “Is this true?” Say, “Yes, by my Lord! Most certainly it is true! And you will have no escape.”
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is asked whether the warning is true and instructed to swear by his Lord that it certainly is. The emphatic reply leaves no ambiguity about the reality of judgment. There will be no escape from what Allah has decreed. The statement counters the assumption that people can evade accountability by denying or delaying it.

phrases.translation: If every wrongdoer were to possess everything in the world, they would surely ransom themselves with it.
phrases.explanation: Even if a wrongdoer owned everything in the world, they would try to offer it as ransom when punishment appears. The verse shows that worldly wealth cannot purchase release from judgment.

phrases.translation: They will hide ˹their˺ remorse when they see the torment. And they will be judged in all fairness, and none will be wronged
phrases.explanation: They conceal their remorse when they see the punishment. Their regret comes only after the consequences become visible, too late to undo the actions that led there. They are judged fairly and no one is wronged. The verse closes by affirming justice even while describing a frightening outcome.

phrases.translation: Surely to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. Surely Allah’s promise is ˹always˺ true, but most of them do not know
phrases.explanation: Everything in the heavens and earth belongs to Allah. The statement grounds the following promise in His complete authority over all creation. Allah’s promise is always true, though many people do not know or recognize it. Lack of awareness does not weaken the promise or make its fulfillment uncertain.

phrases.translation: He ˹is the One Who˺ gives life and causes death, and to Him you will ˹all˺ be returned
phrases.explanation: Allah gives life, causes death, and receives everyone in return. These powers frame human existence from beginning to end and make the promise of resurrection part of His complete authority.

phrases.translation: O humanity! Indeed, there has come to you a warning from your Lord, a cure for what is in the hearts, a guide, and a mercy for the believers
phrases.explanation: A warning has come from the Lord to all humanity. It calls people to take revelation seriously before the consequences it describes arrive. The message is a cure for what troubles the heart. Guidance can correct false beliefs and moral habits, addressing inner disorder rather than only outward behavior. The revelation is a guide and mercy for believers. It offers direction and care to those who respond, helping them live with clarity and hope.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “In Allah’s grace and mercy let them rejoice. That is far better than whatever ˹wealth˺ they amass.”
phrases.explanation: People are told to rejoice in Allah’s grace and mercy. The verse directs joy toward divine generosity and guidance, not merely toward possessions or worldly status. This is better than the wealth people accumulate. Material goods are temporary, while Allah’s mercy and guidance provide a deeper and more lasting good.

phrases.translation: Ask ˹the pagans, O Prophet˺, “Have you seen that which Allah has sent down for you as a provision, of which you have made some lawful and some unlawful?”
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is told to ask the pagans about provision Allah has sent down for them. The question begins with the recognition that sustenance ultimately comes from Allah. They divide that provision into what they declare lawful and unlawful. The verse challenges them to identify the authority behind these religious rulings.

phrases.translation: Say, “Has Allah given you authorization, or are you fabricating lies against Allah?”
phrases.explanation: The Prophet asks whether Allah authorized their declarations or whether they are inventing claims against Him. The warning concerns speaking for Allah without permission, not careful obedience to genuine guidance.

phrases.translation: What do those who fabricate lies against Allah expect on Judgment Day?
phrases.explanation: The verse asks what those who fabricate lies against Allah expect when Judgment Day arrives. Their claims may pass unchallenged for a time, but they will face a final accounting.

phrases.translation: Surely Allah is ever Bountiful to humanity, but most of them are ungrateful
phrases.explanation: Allah is bountiful to humanity, yet many are ungrateful. The contrast shows that rejecting truth is not caused by a lack of divine provision, but by failure to recognize and appreciate it.

phrases.translation: There is no activity you may be engaged in ˹O Prophet˺ or portion of the Quran you may be reciting, nor any deed you ˹all˺ may be doing except that We are a Witness over you while doing it. Not ˹even˺ an atom’s weight is hidden from your Lord on earth or in heaven; nor anything smaller or larger than that, but is ˹written˺ in a perfect Record
phrases.explanation: The verse includes the Prophet’s activities, recitation, and the community’s deeds under Allah’s witness. No action is outside His knowledge, whether it is public or private. Not even an atom’s weight is hidden from Allah on earth or in heaven. The tiny example stresses the completeness of His knowledge across every place and scale. Nothing smaller or larger escapes the perfect Record. The image assures that every deed is preserved accurately and will be available for judgment.

phrases.translation: There will certainly be no fear for the close servants of Allah, nor will they grieve
phrases.explanation: Allah’s close servants will have no fear and will not grieve. The promise describes their safety in the Hereafter, when the anxieties of worldly life no longer trouble them or diminish their joy.

phrases.translation: ˹They are˺ those who are faithful and are mindful ˹of Him˺
phrases.explanation: The close servants are described as faithful and mindful of Allah. Their closeness is tied to belief and reverent conduct, not merely to a special title or claim in daily conduct.

phrases.translation: For them is good news in this worldly life and the Hereafter. There is no change in the promise of Allah. That is ˹truly˺ the ultimate triumph
phrases.explanation: The faithful receive good news in this life and the Hereafter. The promise reaches beyond immediate circumstances, offering hope both now and in the lasting future. Allah’s promise cannot be changed. This certainty gives believers a firm basis for hope even when worldly events seem to contradict the good news. The promise is the ultimate triumph. Success is defined by Allah’s lasting reward, not simply by temporary achievement or recognition.

phrases.translation: Do not let their words grieve you ˹O Prophet˺. Surely all honour and power belongs to Allah. He is the All-Hearing, All-Knowing
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is told not to be distressed by the opponents’ words. Their insults cannot undo the truth or determine the eventual outcome of the message. All honour and power belong to Allah, who hears and knows everything. The reminder directs the Prophet away from seeking validation from opponents and toward trust in his Lord.

phrases.translation: Certainly to Allah ˹alone˺ belong all those in the heavens and all those on the earth. And what do those who associate others with Allah really follow? They follow nothing but assumptions and do nothing but lie
phrases.explanation: Everyone in the heavens and on earth belongs to Allah. The verse reinforces His sole authority before questioning why people direct worship elsewhere. Those who associate partners with Allah rely on assumptions rather than revealed knowledge. Their beliefs do not provide the certainty they claim. They do nothing but lie. The verse condemns the false claims they make about worship and divine authority.

phrases.translation: He is the One Who has made the night for you to rest in and the day bright. Surely in this are signs for people who listen
phrases.explanation: Allah made the night for rest. Its darkness and quiet provide a recurring opportunity for people to recover and recognize the care built into their daily lives. The day is made bright for activity. The balance between night and day is a sign for those willing to listen and reflect on the order around them. These patterns are signs for people who listen. Hearing revelation with attention helps a person connect ordinary rhythms with their Creator.

phrases.translation: They say, “Allah has offspring.” Glory be to Him! He is the Self-Sufficient. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth.
phrases.explanation: Some people claim that Allah has offspring, attributing family relationships to the Creator. The verse immediately rejects this claim and reminds them of Allah’s complete independence. Allah is self-sufficient and owns everything in the heavens and earth. His complete ownership means He has no need for offspring or partners.

phrases.translation: You have no proof of this! Do you say about Allah what you do not know
phrases.explanation: The claim has no proof. The verse asks people not to treat an inherited assertion as knowledge when they cannot establish its truth. They are challenged for speaking about Allah without knowledge. The warning calls for care and humility in claims about God.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Indeed, those who fabricate lies against Allah will never succeed.”
phrases.explanation: Those who invent lies about Allah will never succeed. The statement warns against false religious claims and denies that temporary influence can make them ultimately successful or secure in the Hereafter.

phrases.translation: ˹It is only˺ a brief enjoyment in this world, then to Us is their return, then We will make them taste the severe punishment for their disbelief
phrases.explanation: The enjoyment of this world is brief. The verse places present pleasure in perspective without denying that it exists, emphasizing that it is not the final outcome. The disbelievers return to Allah after their worldly life. Their return makes accountability unavoidable, however secure they may have felt in life. They will taste severe punishment for disbelief. The verse links this outcome to their rejection and the choices described throughout the passage.

phrases.translation: Relate to them ˹O Prophet˺ the story of Noah when he said to his people, “O my People! If my presence and my reminders to you of Allah’s signs are unbearable to you, then ˹know that˺ I have put my trust in Allah.
phrases.explanation: Noah tells his people that if his presence and reminders of Allah’s signs are intolerable, he still will not abandon his duty. The message is delivered despite their hostility. Noah places his trust in Allah. His confidence does not depend on the people accepting him or on his ability to control their response.

phrases.translation: So devise a plot along with your associate-gods—and you do not have to be secretive about your plot—then carry it out against me without delay
phrases.explanation: He openly challenges them to devise their plan with their associate-gods and not hide it. His words express complete reliance, not a call for the Prophet’s audience to imitate conflict. Noah tells them to carry out their plan without delay. The challenge exposes his fearlessness before people who threaten him and sets up the contrast with their eventual rejection.

phrases.translation: And if you turn away, ˹remember˺ I have never demanded a reward from you ˹for delivering the message˺. My reward is only from Allah. And I have been commanded to be one of those who submit ˹to Allah˺.”
phrases.explanation: Noah says he has never asked his people for a payment in exchange for delivering the message. His role is not a way to gain wealth or personal advantage. His reward comes from Allah alone. The statement emphasizes sincerity and freedom from financial motives. Noah has been commanded to be among those who submit to Allah. His own obedience is the foundation of the message he conveys.

phrases.translation: But they still rejected him, so We saved him and those with him in the Ark and made them successors,
phrases.explanation: Noah’s people reject him despite his warning. Their response repeats the pattern of turning away from a messenger sent to guide them. Allah saves Noah and those with him in the Ark and makes them successors in the land. The rescue shows that the rejection of the majority does not defeat Allah’s plan.

phrases.translation: and drowned those who rejected Our signs. See then what was the end of those who had been warned
phrases.explanation: Those who reject Allah’s signs are drowned. The verse states the consequence that follows their refusal after being warned. The audience is asked to consider the end of those who were warned. Noah’s story serves as a lesson about the consequences of persistent denial.

phrases.translation: Then after him We sent ˹other˺ messengers to their ˹own˺ people and they came to them with clear proofs. But they would not believe in what they had rejected before. This is how We seal the hearts of the transgressors
phrases.explanation: After Noah, Allah sends other messengers to their own peoples with clear proofs. The repeated mission shows that communities continue to receive guidance after earlier generations. The later peoples refuse to believe in what they had already rejected. Repetition deepens their responsibility because they persist in the same denial. Allah seals the hearts of transgressors. The verse portrays this as the outcome of continued rejection, not as a barrier placed before an otherwise sincere seeker.

phrases.translation: Then after these ˹messengers˺ We sent Moses and Aaron to Pharaoh and his chiefs with Our signs. But they behaved arrogantly and were a wicked people
phrases.explanation: Moses and Aaron are sent to Pharaoh and his chiefs with Allah’s signs. Their mission brings guidance directly to the rulers and their political circle. Pharaoh and his chiefs respond with arrogance. Their authority becomes a reason to resist the signs rather than an opportunity to act justly. They are described as a wicked people. The judgment follows their response to the messengers and the guidance they were given.

phrases.translation: When the truth came to them from Us, they said, “This is certainly pure magic!”
phrases.explanation: When truth comes from Allah, Pharaoh’s people call it magic. The accusation shows how those committed to rejecting guidance can reinterpret clear evidence as deception. They insist that the truth is pure magic. Their label avoids answering the message itself and prepares the confrontation with Moses that follows.

phrases.translation: Moses responded, “Is this what you say about the truth when it has come to you? Is this magic? Magicians will never succeed.”
phrases.explanation: Moses asks whether they call the truth magic after it has reached them. His question exposes their refusal to consider the message fairly. He repeats their accusation as a question, challenging them to examine what they are saying rather than use the label to dismiss him. Magicians will never succeed. Moses rejects the claim that truth is magic and warns that deception cannot secure lasting success.

phrases.translation: They argued, “Have you come to turn us away from the faith of our forefathers
phrases.explanation: Pharaoh’s people accuse Moses and Aaron of turning them away from ancestral religion. Their appeal to tradition is used to resist a message they have not answered on its merits.

phrases.translation: so that the two of you may become supreme in the land? We will never believe in you!”
phrases.explanation: They suggest that the brothers seek political dominance. This accusation shifts attention from the truth of their message to an alleged personal motive. They declare that they will never believe. The statement reveals their determination to reject the messengers before the dispute is resolved.

phrases.translation: Pharaoh demanded, “Bring me every skilled magician.”
phrases.explanation: Pharaoh orders that every skilled magician be brought to him. He responds to Moses’ message by assembling experts for a public contest, turning the dispute into a test before the people.

phrases.translation: When the magicians came, Moses said to them, “Cast whatever you wish to cast!”
phrases.explanation: When the magicians arrive, Moses tells them to cast what they choose. His calm invitation shows confidence that the truth will not depend on hiding from a public challenge before the assembled audience.

phrases.translation: When they did, Moses said, “What you have produced is mere magic, Allah will surely make it useless, for Allah certainly does not set right the work of the corruptors
phrases.explanation: After the magicians cast their display, Moses calls it magic and says Allah will make it ineffective. The verse denies that corruptors can make deception prevail when Allah establishes the truth.

phrases.translation: And Allah establishes the truth by His Words—even to the dismay of the wicked.”
phrases.explanation: Allah establishes the truth by His words, even when wicked people dislike the result. The promise reassures Moses and his followers that opposition cannot finally overturn divine guidance. This assures them that evil will not prevail permanently.

phrases.translation: But no one believed in Moses except a few youths of his people, while fearing that Pharaoh and their own chiefs might persecute them.
phrases.explanation: Only a few young people from Moses’ community believe in him. Their small number reflects the danger of openly opposing Pharaoh, not a lack of clarity in the message. The believers fear persecution from Pharaoh and even from their own chiefs. The verse shows the social pressure surrounding early faith under an oppressive ruler.

phrases.translation: And certainly Pharaoh was a tyrant in the land, and he was truly a transgressor
phrases.explanation: Pharaoh is described as a tyrant in the land. Political power is being used to intimidate people and obstruct their freedom to believe. He is truly a transgressor. The verse names his conduct as unjust excess, setting the context for Moses’ instruction to trust Allah.

phrases.translation: Moses said, “O my people! If you do believe in Allah and submit ˹to His Will˺, then put your trust in Him.”
phrases.explanation: Moses tells his people that belief and submission should lead them to trust Allah. Trust is a response to faith, especially when fear of persecution makes the future uncertain. Their safety is not fully in their own hands.

phrases.translation: They replied, “In Allah we trust. Our Lord! Do not subject us to the persecution of the oppressive people
phrases.explanation: The people answer that they trust Allah and ask not to be made victims of oppressive people. Their prayer shows that reliance on Allah can include asking for protection from injustice.

phrases.translation: and deliver us by Your mercy from the disbelieving people.”
phrases.explanation: They ask Allah to deliver them by His mercy from the disbelieving people. The prayer combines trust with a request for rescue from a community that persecutes them under Pharaoh’s rule.

phrases.translation: We revealed to Moses and his brother, “Appoint houses for your people in Egypt. Turn these houses into places of worship,
phrases.explanation: Moses and Aaron are instructed to appoint houses for their people in Egypt. The homes provide an organized base for a community living under Pharaoh’s rule. The houses are to become places of worship. The instruction turns ordinary homes into spaces where the community can gather around faith.

phrases.translation: establish prayer, and give good news to the believers!”
phrases.explanation: They are told to establish prayer. Regular worship keeps the community connected to Allah during a period of political pressure. The believers are given good news. The command pairs practical arrangements and worship with hope in Allah’s care.

phrases.translation: Moses prayed, “Our Lord! You have granted Pharaoh and his chiefs luxuries and riches in this worldly life, ˹which they abused˺ to lead people astray from Your Way!
phrases.explanation: Moses acknowledges that Pharaoh and his chiefs have received luxuries and riches. Their prosperity is not evidence of righteousness, especially when they use their position against others. Moses says the rulers abuse their wealth to lead people away from Allah’s way. The verse connects material power with the responsibility not to manipulate or misguide others.

phrases.translation: Our Lord, destroy their riches and harden their hearts
phrases.explanation: Moses prays for the rulers’ riches to be destroyed and their hearts hardened. This severe plea comes in the context of Pharaoh’s sustained oppression and rejection after signs, not as a general model for responding to disagreement.

phrases.translation: so that they will not believe until they see the painful punishment.”
phrases.explanation: He asks that they remain in disbelief until they see painful punishment. The prayer reflects the long conflict with an entrenched tyrant and the certainty that his abuse will face judgment.

phrases.translation: Allah responded ˹to Moses and Aaron˺, “Your prayer is answered! So be steadfast and do not follow the way of those who do not know.”
phrases.explanation: Allah tells Moses and Aaron that their prayer has been answered. The response confirms that their appeal has been heard, though its fulfillment follows Allah’s timing. They are told to remain steadfast and not follow those who do not know. Patience and guidance matter while waiting for the outcome of their confrontation with Pharaoh.

phrases.translation: We brought the Children of Israel across the sea. Then Pharaoh and his soldiers pursued them unjustly and oppressively. But as Pharaoh was drowning, he cried out, “I believe that there is no god except that in whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am ˹now˺ one of those who submit.”
phrases.explanation: The Children of Israel cross the sea and escape Pharaoh’s pursuit. The event marks a dramatic deliverance from a ruler who had tried to keep them oppressed. Pharaoh and his soldiers pursue them unjustly and oppressively. Their power is used to chase people who are fleeing, exposing the injustice behind the pursuit. As he drowns, Pharaoh declares belief in the God of Israel and says he submits. His confession comes only when death is upon him, after a life of disobedience.

phrases.translation: ˹He was told,˺ “Now ˹you believe˺? But you always disobeyed and were one of the corruptors
phrases.explanation: Pharaoh is challenged for waiting until the moment of drowning to claim belief. The question distinguishes a last-second admission under unavoidable punishment from a sincere response while there was time to change. He had persistently disobeyed and corrupted the land. The reminder connects his final confession to the long pattern of injustice that preceded it.

phrases.translation: Today We will preserve your corpse so that you may become an example for those who come after you. And surely most people are heedless of Our examples!”
phrases.explanation: Pharaoh’s corpse is preserved as an example for later people. The image makes the end of a powerful ruler visible and warns that worldly authority cannot defeat Allah. Most people remain heedless of such examples. A visible lesson only benefits those who pause to reflect and change their conduct.

phrases.translation: Indeed, We settled the Children of Israel in a blessed land, and granted them good, lawful provisions. They did not differ until knowledge came to them. Surely your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Judgment regarding their differences
phrases.explanation: Allah settles the Children of Israel in a blessed land and provides them with good, lawful sustenance. The verse describes care for the community after its deliverance. They do not differ until knowledge reaches them. The verse points to disagreement arising among people who have received guidance, rather than from an absence of revelation. Allah will judge between them on the Day of Judgment regarding their differences. Final resolution belongs to Him, who knows the truth and each person’s responsibility.

phrases.translation: If you ˹O Prophet˺ are in doubt about ˹these stories˺ that We have revealed to you,
phrases.explanation: The verse uses a conditional address to the Prophet about doubt concerning the revealed stories. It does not say he actually doubts. The wording emphasizes the certainty of the account.

phrases.translation: then ask those who read the Scripture before you. The truth has certainly come to you from your Lord, so do not be one of those who doubt
phrases.explanation: Readers of earlier Scripture are named as witnesses who can confirm that revelation and prophetic history did not begin with this community. The truth has come from Allah, so the Prophet is told not to be among those who doubt. The statement reinforces the message’s certainty and steadies its hearers.

phrases.translation: and do not be one of those who deny Allah’s signs or you will be one of the losers
phrases.explanation: The warning continues: do not deny Allah’s signs, or you will be among the losers. Rejection is presented as a choice with real consequences, not a harmless disagreement. The warning continues the previous call to keep faith.

phrases.translation: Indeed, those against whom Allah’s decree ˹of torment˺ is justified will not believe—
phrases.explanation: Those against whom Allah’s decree of punishment is justified will not believe. The verse describes people whose persistent rejection has become settled, linking the outcome with their continued resistance. This describes the result of repeated rejection.

phrases.translation: even if every sign were to come to them—until they see the painful punishment
phrases.explanation: Even every sign would not make them believe before painful punishment arrives. The verse warns that evidence cannot help people who have decided to refuse it until consequences become unavoidable.

phrases.translation: If only there had been a society which believed ˹before seeing the torment˺ and, therefore, benefited from its belief, like the people of Jonah.
phrases.explanation: The verse asks why no society believed before seeing punishment and benefited from faith. The question introduces a rare contrast to the communities that waited too long. The people of Jonah are given as the example of a community that believed in time. Their response distinguishes them from those who only acknowledge truth after punishment arrives.

phrases.translation: When they believed, We lifted from them the torment of disgrace in this world and allowed them enjoyment for a while
phrases.explanation: When they believed, Allah lifted the disgraceful torment from them. Their change of direction leads to relief rather than the destruction faced by other rejecting peoples. Allah allows them enjoyment for a while. The temporary reprieve shows mercy toward a community that turns back before its opportunity is gone.

phrases.translation: Had your Lord so willed ˹O Prophet˺, all ˹people˺ on earth would have certainly believed, every single one of them! Would you then force people to become believers
phrases.explanation: If Allah had willed, everyone on earth could have believed. The verse makes clear that universal faith is within His power, while people do not all respond in the same way. The Prophet is asked whether he would force people to become believers. He is responsible for conveying guidance, not compelling faith or controlling another person’s heart.

phrases.translation: It is not for any soul to believe except by Allah’s leave, and He will bring His wrath upon those who are unmindful
phrases.explanation: No soul believes except by Allah’s leave. The verse places faith within divine authority while the surrounding passage continues to hold people accountable for how they respond to guidance. Allah brings wrath upon those who are unmindful. The warning links heedlessness with a serious consequence and calls people to attend to the signs and message they have received.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Consider all that is in the heavens and the earth!” Yet neither signs nor warners are of any benefit to those who refuse to believe
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is told to invite people to consider everything in the heavens and earth. Creation offers signs of Allah’s power, but observing signs alone cannot help someone determined to refuse belief. Signs and warners do not benefit those who refuse to believe. The verse distinguishes a lack of evidence from a deliberate unwillingness to respond to it.

phrases.translation: Are they waiting for ˹anything˺ except the same torments that befell those before them? Say, “Keep waiting then! I too am waiting with you.”
phrases.explanation: The question asks whether the opponents are waiting for the same punishment that came to earlier peoples. Their delay does not make the warning less serious or the outcome less possible. The Prophet tells them to keep waiting, while he too waits. The reply rejects their demand for proof on their terms and leaves the outcome to Allah’s judgment.

phrases.translation: Then We saved Our messengers and those who believed. For it is Our duty to save the believers
phrases.explanation: Allah saves His messengers and those who believe with them. The verse recalls a repeated pattern in which truth is not finally defeated by the hostility of its opponents. Saving the believers is described as Allah’s duty, meaning a promise He has made through His mercy. It assures believers that His commitment to them is dependable.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “O humanity! If you are in doubt of my faith, then ˹know that˺ I do not worship those ˹idols˺ you worship instead of Allah.
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is told to address all humanity and state that he does not worship the idols they worship besides Allah. The conditional wording about doubt is a challenge, not a claim that he actually doubts.

phrases.translation: But I worship Allah, Who has the power to cause your death. And I have been commanded, ‘Be one of the believers,’
phrases.explanation: He worships Allah, who has power over their lives and deaths. The contrast directs worship to the One with real authority rather than to powerless objects. The Prophet is commanded to be one of the believers. His message is grounded in the same submission and faith he calls others to embrace.

phrases.translation: and, ‘Be steadfast in faith in all uprightness, and do not be one of the polytheists,’
phrases.explanation: The command is to remain steadfast in faith with uprightness. Belief is not merely a declaration but a direction that should shape a person’s conduct consistently. He must not be among the polytheists. The instruction reinforces exclusive worship of Allah and rejects associating partners with Him.

phrases.translation: and ‘Do not invoke, instead of Allah, what can neither benefit nor harm you—for if you do, then you will certainly be one of the wrongdoers,’
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is told not to invoke anything besides Allah that cannot bring benefit or prevent harm. The verse challenges the practice of seeking ultimate help from powerless idols. Invoking such beings would make a person one of the wrongdoers. The warning connects worship with responsibility and calls people to direct devotion to Allah alone.

phrases.translation: and ‘If Allah touches you with harm, none can undo it except Him. And if He intends good for you, none can withhold His bounty.
phrases.explanation: If harm touches a person, none can remove it except Allah. The verse denies that any created being has independent power to overturn what Allah allows. If Allah intends good, no one can withhold His bounty. Together with the warning about harm, this assures believers that ultimate outcomes rest with Allah.

phrases.translation: He grants it to whoever He wills of His servants. And He is the All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.’”
phrases.explanation: Allah grants His bounty to whichever servants He wills. The verse presents provision as an expression of divine generosity, not something people can control completely. Allah is All-Forgiving and Most Merciful. These qualities balance the warning about harm with hope, reminding people that they can seek forgiveness and mercy.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “O humanity! The truth has surely come to you from your Lord. So whoever chooses to be guided, it is only for their own good.
phrases.explanation: The truth has come to humanity from Allah. The verse presents guidance as a gift already delivered, inviting people to respond rather than wait for a different message. Choosing guidance benefits the person who accepts it. Faith is not a favor owed to the Prophet but a path whose good returns to the believer.

phrases.translation: And whoever chooses to stray, it is only to their own loss. And I am not a keeper over you.”
phrases.explanation: Choosing to stray harms the person who rejects guidance. The verse makes individual responsibility clear without suggesting that the Prophet can control people’s choices. The Prophet is not appointed as a keeper over them. His task is to convey the truth, not to compel belief or take responsibility for another person’s response.

phrases.translation: And follow what is revealed to you, and be patient until Allah passes His judgment. For He is the Best of Judges
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is instructed to follow revelation and remain patient until Allah gives judgment. The command encourages steadfastness through opposition rather than rushing to control the outcome. Allah is the Best of Judges. The final decision belongs to the One whose knowledge and justice are complete, giving the Prophet a reason to trust the outcome.
